scroll_of_cure_wounds.name: scroll of cure wounds
scroll_of_cure_wounds.lore: The prophet Jeremiah asked whether there was no balm in Gilead, the hill country whose fragrant resin caravans carried down to Egypt as medicine. Apprentice healers copy a short blessing over the balm onto cheap parchment. Read aloud, it closes a cut and steadies the reader, and little more.

scroll_of_healing.name: scroll of healing
scroll_of_healing.lore: At Salerno, on the coast south of Naples, Europe's first medical school taught from Greek, Latin, Arabic and Hebrew books, and admitted women among its teachers. Its masters wrote their best remedies as verses so that students would remember them. This is one such verse, and it mends an honest wound.

scroll_of_vigor.name: scroll of vigor
scroll_of_vigor.lore: The abbess Hildegard of Bingen wrote two books of medicine in the twelfth century and gave a name to the force she saw in sap and in healthy flesh alike: viriditas, the greening power. This rite calls on it. Wounds close over like a tree healing around a nail.

scroll_of_rejuvenation.name: scroll of rejuvenation
scroll_of_rejuvenation.lore: Jason's father Aeson was old and failing, and Medea took nine nights to gather herbs by chariot. She drained the old man's blood, filled his veins with her brew, and he rose forty years younger. The olive stick she stirred with had sprouted leaves. This rite restores a badly broken body in one reading.

scroll_of_full_restoration.name: scroll of full restoration
scroll_of_full_restoration.lore: Raphael means 'God heals'. In the Book of Tobit the archangel travelled in disguise as a hired guide and at the journey's end taught Tobias to cure his father's blindness with the gall of a fish. The old man saw his son and wept. This is the greatest of the healing rites, and death hesitates over its reader.

scroll_of_local_mapping.name: scroll of local mapping
scroll_of_local_mapping.lore: Ariadne gave Theseus a ball of thread before he entered the Labyrinth. He tied one end to the door, killed the Minotaur at the centre, and followed the thread out. A surveyor's rough shorthand does the thread's work for the ground close by: a few dozen paces of passage, drawn in the mind.

scroll_of_area_mapping.name: scroll of area mapping
scroll_of_area_mapping.lore: Roman surveyors laid out roads and camps with the groma, a staff topped by a cross with a plumb line at each arm. Sighting along two lines gave a perfect right angle, which is why their towns are still square. A journeyman's scroll sights down the corridors the same way, a good distance in every direction.

scroll_of_cartography.name: scroll of cartography
scroll_of_cartography.lore: Medieval pilots sailed by portolan charts, drawn on a single calfskin with every harbour named along the coast and a web of compass lines crossing the sea. The oldest to survive, the Carta Pisana, is from about 1290. The scroll draws the passages like such a coast, well past the next several bends.

scroll_of_deep_mapping.name: scroll of deep mapping
scroll_of_deep_mapping.lore: On Samos in the sixth century before Christ, the engineer Eupalinos drove a water tunnel a full kilometre through a mountain. Two crews dug from opposite sides and met in the middle, almost exactly. The scroll holds that kind of knowledge of rock. Room by room, nearly all of a level takes shape.

scroll_of_dungeon_mapping.name: scroll of dungeon mapping
scroll_of_dungeon_mapping.lore: About 1300 a cleric drew the whole world on one calfskin for Hereford Cathedral: Jerusalem at the centre, Paradise at the top, and hundreds of towns, beasts and marvels between. It hangs there still. This scroll is as ambitious about a single floor, and it is more accurate. Every corridor and stair appears at once.

scroll_of_identify.name: scroll of identify
scroll_of_identify.lore: Lydian goldsmiths tested a coin by rubbing it on a slab of black stone and reading the colour of the streak. They called the slab a touchstone, and it could not be fooled. The ink of this scroll is ground from the same idea. It gives the true name and nature of one chosen thing.

scroll_of_identify_two.name: scroll of identify two
scroll_of_identify_two.lore: Two women came before Solomon with one living child, each swearing it was hers. He called for a sword to divide the baby, and the true mother cried out to give it up. He knew her by that. This scroll settles two questions at a sitting: the first pair of unknown things in the pack are named.

scroll_of_identify_three.name: scroll of identify three
scroll_of_identify_three.lore: A hand appeared at Belshazzar's feast and wrote on the plaster. None of Babylon's wise men could read it. Daniel could: three words, numbered, weighed, divided, and the kingdom fell that night. An appraiser's stock scroll reads three unknown things as plainly, and names them honestly.

scroll_of_mass_identify.name: scroll of mass identify
scroll_of_mass_identify.lore: Before there was any other work to do, God brought every beast of the field and bird of the air to Adam to see what he would call them, and whatever he called each one, that was its name. This rite runs the same parade through a pack. Every unnamed thing in it is named.

scroll_of_omnisight.name: scroll of omnisight
scroll_of_omnisight.lore: Argus Panoptes, the all-seeing, had a hundred eyes and never closed more than a few at once. When Hermes killed him, Hera set the eyes in the peacock's tail. This rite opens all of them. Every hidden name in the pack is read, and one carcass among the baggage gives up its lore as well.

scroll_of_sharpen.name: scroll of sharpen
scroll_of_sharpen.lore: Odin, travelling in disguise, showed nine farmhands a whetstone that put a finer edge on their scythes than any other. All nine wanted it. He tossed it in the air and they cut one another down reaching for it. A smith's first scroll is weaker. It takes on a blade only when the parchment itself has been blessed.

scroll_of_weapon_blessing.name: scroll of weapon blessing
scroll_of_weapon_blessing.lore: The old pontificals include a blessing of the sword, read over a new knight's blade before it was belted on, asking that it defend churches, widows and orphans. A temple armourer copied the prayer here. The weapon in hand comes away keener and truer than the smith left it.

scroll_of_enchant_weapon.name: scroll of enchant weapon
scroll_of_enchant_weapon.lore: Between the ninth and eleventh centuries, Frankish smiths sold swords with a name inlaid in iron down the blade: Ulfberht, between two crosses. The steel was so good that forgers copied the name and misspelled it. This scroll writes a true inscription. Both the blade in hand and the bow on the back take it.

scroll_of_weaponsmith.name: scroll of the weaponsmith
scroll_of_weaponsmith.lore: King Nidud cut the hamstrings of Wayland the Smith and kept him on an island to forge for the crown. Wayland made the king marvellous things, took his revenge, and flew away on wings of his own making. Beowulf's mail shirt was called Wayland's work. So is this rite, which betters every weapon carried, and betters it twice.

scroll_of_legendary_edge.name: scroll of the legendary edge
scroll_of_legendary_edge.lore: Odin drove the sword Gram into a tree and only Sigmund could draw it. It broke in his last battle, and the smith Regin reforged the pieces for Sigmund's son. Sigurd tested it by splitting the anvil to its base, then by cutting a tuft of wool that drifted against it in a stream. This rite gives that edge.

scroll_of_bracing.name: scroll of bracing
scroll_of_bracing.lore: Saul dressed the boy David in the royal bronze helmet and coat of mail. David took a few steps, said he could not go in armour he had not proved, and took it all off. An armourer's bracing-rite fits a piece of kit to its wearer. It holds only when the parchment has been blessed.

scroll_of_armor_blessing.name: scroll of armor blessing
scroll_of_armor_blessing.lore: On the night before he was knighted, a squire bathed, put on white, and laid his armour on the altar. He kept watch over it on his knees until morning. A temple armourer wrote down the blessing spoken at dawn. Read over worn harness, it strengthens a couple of pieces.

scroll_of_enchant_armor.name: scroll of enchant armor
scroll_of_enchant_armor.lore: Before Beowulf sailed to face Grendel, he asked one thing of his king: if he died, send home his mail shirt, because Wayland had made it. A guild scroll cannot promise Wayland, but it makes a fair copy of his method. Several pieces of worn armour are drawn tighter and harder.

scroll_of_armorer.name: scroll of the armorer
scroll_of_armorer.lore: In the fifteenth century the Missaglia family of Milan made plate so well fitted that princes sent their measurements across the Alps rather than trust a local smith. Their mark was struck into every piece. This rite carries a master's mark. Most of a harness is reinforced, and well.

scroll_of_legendary_ward.name: scroll of the legendary ward
scroll_of_legendary_ward.lore: No weapon could pierce the Nemean lion, so Heracles strangled it. He then found that no knife would skin it either, until he thought to use the beast's own claws. He wore the hide for the rest of his life. The greatest armourer's rite makes every worn piece nearly that stubborn.

scroll_of_uncurse.name: scroll of uncurse
scroll_of_uncurse.lore: Monks who wanted rid of their abbot handed Benedict of Nursia a cup of poisoned wine. He made the sign of the cross over it, as he did before every meal, and the cup shattered. An acolyte's rite copies the gesture. One cursed thing the reader is wearing lets go.

scroll_of_purity.name: scroll of purity
scroll_of_purity.lore: Before Sunday Mass the priest walks the nave sprinkling the people with blessed water, while the choir sings the psalm verse about being washed whiter than snow. The rite is called the Asperges, after its first word. A monastic copy does the same for gear. Everything cursed that the reader wears is released.

scroll_of_cleansing.name: scroll of cleansing
scroll_of_cleansing.lore: On the Day of Atonement the high priest laid both hands on a live goat, confessed over it the sins of all Israel, and sent it away into the wilderness. English calls it the scapegoat. An exorcist's rite loads a burden and drives it off the same way: curses fall from worn gear and afflictions from the body.

scroll_of_purification.name: scroll of purification
scroll_of_purification.lore: The Egyptians buried their dead with a papyrus they called the Book of Coming Forth by Day. Its longest spell is a list of forty-two denials, one for each judge in the hall where the heart is weighed against a feather. This liturgy pleads as thoroughly. Every cursed thing carried, worn or stowed, is unbound.

scroll_of_sanctification.name: scroll of sanctification
scroll_of_sanctification.lore: Isaiah saw the Lord enthroned and cried that he was a man of unclean lips. A seraph flew to him with a live coal taken from the altar with tongs, touched his mouth, and his guilt was gone. This rite does not stop at cleansing either. Every curse lifts, and one worn piece is left blessed.

scroll_of_ward.name: scroll of ward
scroll_of_ward.lore: The Law told Israel to write its words on the doorposts of the house. To this day a small case holding a strip of parchment, the mezuzah, is fixed to the right side of a Jewish door. A watchman's charm works on that principle. A thin guard settles on the reader and soon fades.

scroll_of_protection.name: scroll of protection
scroll_of_protection.lore: The prayer called Saint Patrick's Breastplate binds its speaker to the strength of heaven: Christ before, behind, beneath, above, on the right hand and the left. Tradition says Patrick sang it on the road to Tara and his enemies saw only deer go by. Temple acolytes copy it out. The words close around the reader.

scroll_of_greater_protection.name: scroll of greater protection
scroll_of_greater_protection.lore: The ninety-first Psalm promises that no terror by night nor arrow by day will come near the one who trusts. For two thousand years people have worn it: on scraps of papyrus, in lockets, sewn into soldiers' coats. This rite is the Psalm written in full by a careful hand, and the guard it raises lasts.

scroll_of_aegis.name: scroll of aegis
scroll_of_aegis.lore: Hephaestus made the aegis for Zeus: a goatskin fringed with a hundred golden tassels, with the Gorgon's head at its centre. Athena wore it into battle more often than her father did, and not even his thunderbolt could break it. Her temple scribes wrote this rite. Ordinary blades find no purchase on its reader.

scroll_of_absolute_ward.name: scroll of absolute ward
scroll_of_absolute_ward.lore: Nebuchadnezzar heated his furnace seven times hotter than usual and threw in Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, bound. The king looked and saw four men walking loose in the fire. The three came out with not a hair singed and no smell of smoke on their coats. This is the longest and strongest of the warding rites.

scroll_of_bewilderment.name: scroll of bewilderment
scroll_of_bewilderment.lore: In July 1518 a woman called Frau Troffea began to dance in a Strasbourg street and could not stop. Within a month hundreds had joined her. The council hired pipers and built a stage, which did not help. A tavern conjurer's scroll passes on a mild case. Every enemy in sight staggers for a moment.

scroll_of_confusion.name: scroll of confusion
scroll_of_confusion.lore: Odysseus told the Cyclops his name was Nobody. When the blinded giant screamed for help, his neighbours called through the rock to ask who was hurting him. Nobody, he roared, and they told him to pray and went back to bed. This rite sows that much muddle among every enemy in view.

scroll_of_madness.name: scroll of madness
scroll_of_madness.lore: King Pentheus forbade the worship of Dionysus in Thebes. The god sent the king's own mother into the hills with the dancing women, and when Pentheus crept up to spy, she took him for a mountain lion. She carried her trophy home before her eyes cleared. This working unmoors every creature in sight, and for a long while.

scroll_of_drowsing.name: scroll of drowsing
scroll_of_drowsing.lore: A dragon that never slept guarded the Golden Fleece. Medea walked up to it singing, dipped a sprig of fresh-cut juniper in her potion, and sprinkled its eyes until the great head sank. Jason took the Fleece off the oak. A soothing-charm in her manner makes everything in sight nod, briefly.

scroll_of_sleep.name: scroll of sleep
scroll_of_sleep.lore: Ovid put the house of Sleep in a cave the sun never enters. The river Lethe murmurs over pebbles at its foot, poppies grow at the mouth, and there is no door, in case a hinge should creak. The scroll's ink is pressed from those poppies. Every creature in sight goes down together.

scroll_of_deep_slumber.name: scroll of deep slumber
scroll_of_deep_slumber.lore: Seven young Christians of Ephesus hid in a cave from the emperor Decius, who had the entrance walled up. They woke when a farmer broke the wall, and sent one of their number to buy bread with coins nearly two centuries old. This working lays a shadow of that sleep on all in view.

scroll_of_quickness.name: scroll of quickness
scroll_of_quickness.lore: When the Persians landed at Marathon, Athens sent the runner Pheidippides to ask Sparta for help. Herodotus says he covered the distance, about a hundred and fifty miles of mountain road, by the second day. A courier's charm lends his legs for a short stretch: two strides in the time of one.

scroll_of_haste.name: scroll of haste
scroll_of_haste.lore: After the fire fell on Carmel, Elijah warned King Ahab to harness his chariot before the rain stopped him. Then the hand of the Lord came on the prophet. He tucked his cloak into his belt and ran ahead of the horses all the way to Jezreel. The scroll gives that run to its reader.

scroll_of_alacrity.name: scroll of alacrity
scroll_of_alacrity.lore: Virgil says the warrior maiden Camilla ran so lightly that she could cross a field of standing wheat without bending an ear, and skim the sea without wetting her feet. She led the cavalry of the Volsci against Aeneas. The greatest of the speed rites lasts far longer than any other.

scroll_of_blink.name: scroll of blink
scroll_of_blink.lore: The prophet Habakkuk was carrying stew to the reapers in Judea when an angel took him by the hair and set him down in Babylon, beside the lions' den where Daniel sat hungry. He handed over the dinner and was returned. An apprentice's scroll moves its reader as abruptly. It does not say where.

scroll_of_teleportation.name: scroll of teleportation
scroll_of_teleportation.lore: The Phaeacians owned ships that needed no helmsman, because the ships knew every harbour and steered by thought. One carried Odysseus home in a single night. The crew laid him asleep on the beach of Ithaca and were gone by dawn. This working is as sure: it sets its reader down somewhere already walked.

scroll_of_recall.name: scroll of recall
scroll_of_recall.lore: The Sibyl told Aeneas that the road down to Avernus is easy, for the door of the dark stands open night and day. Getting back up is the labour. The surveyors of the deep caves took her at her word. Space folds, and the reader stands at the head of the stairs going down.

scroll_of_spark.name: scroll of spark
scroll_of_spark.lore: In the 1780s Luigi Galvani touched a dissected frog's leg with two different metals and it kicked. He thought he had found the animal's own vital spark. An artificer's apprentice-charm passes a twitch of that sort into tired wands. The two most spent in the pack each regain a little.

scroll_of_charging.name: scroll of charging
scroll_of_charging.lore: Alessandro Volta doubted Galvani's frogs and in 1800 stacked discs of zinc and silver between brine-soaked card. The pile gave a steady current, and Napoleon made him a count for it. The unit of electrical pressure bears his name. This rite stacks the discs afresh: every wand carried gains a charge.

scroll_of_recharge.name: scroll of recharge
scroll_of_recharge.lore: In a famine, a widow of Zarephath shared her last handful of flour and last drop of oil with Elijah. From that day the jar of flour was never emptied and the jug of oil never ran dry until the rains came. The great working fills every wand in the pack to its brim.

scroll_of_light.name: scroll of light
scroll_of_light.lore: Hero was a priestess at Sestos, and every night she set a lamp in her tower window so that Leander could swim the Hellespont to her by its light. A candle-lighter's cantrip sets out the same lamp. A soft glow spreads from the reader and shows a good half of the floor.

scroll_of_illumination.name: scroll of illumination
scroll_of_illumination.lore: Sostratus of Cnidus built the Pharos of Alexandria about 280 years before Christ: three tiers of pale stone, among the tallest buildings on earth, with a fire at the top that ships saw some thirty miles out. This rite lights a floor from end to end, and briefly shows what moves on it.

scroll_of_revelation.name: scroll of revelation
scroll_of_revelation.lore: Lynceus sailed with the Argonauts as their lookout because his eyes could see through the trunk of an oak and into the ground beneath it. From a mountain top he once spotted a man hiding inside a hollow tree. The greatest light-working gives his sight for a long while: the whole floor, and every living thing on it.

scroll_of_enchant_ring.name: scroll of enchant ring
scroll_of_enchant_ring.lore: Eligius was a goldsmith so honest that when King Clotaire gave him gold for one throne he made two and handed back both. He became a bishop, and jewellers still keep his feast. The rite is his workmanship. A pair of worn trinkets are each made a little more than they were.

scroll_of_trinketry.name: scroll of trinketry
scroll_of_trinketry.lore: Polycrates of Samos had such unbroken luck that a friend warned him to throw away what he valued most. He rowed out and dropped his emerald signet into the sea. Days later a fisherman brought him a fine fish as a gift, and the ring was inside it. This rite improves a few worn pieces as stubbornly.

scroll_of_master_trinketry.name: scroll of master trinketry
scroll_of_master_trinketry.lore: The dwarf brothers Brokkr and Sindri made the gold arm-ring Draupnir for Odin. Every ninth night eight new rings of equal weight drip from it. Odin laid it on Baldr's pyre, and Baldr sent it back from the land of the dead. Under this working every ring and amulet worn takes a share of that plenty.

scroll_of_enchantment.name: scroll of enchantment
scroll_of_enchantment.lore: When Israel built the Tabernacle in the desert, the Lord named the craftsman: Bezalel of Judah, filled with skill to work gold, silver and bronze, to cut stones and to carve wood. A universal rite needs hands like his, good at everything. A few pieces of worn gear, of any kind, are improved.

scroll_of_greater_enchantment.name: scroll of greater enchantment
scroll_of_greater_enchantment.lore: Loki wagered his own head that the dwarf Brokkr could not match the treasures of the sons of Ivaldi, then turned into a fly and bit the smith's eyelid at the bellows. Brokkr won anyway, with a hammer whose handle came out short. The greater rite has a dwarf's thoroughness: a good share of the kit, well bettered.

scroll_of_grand_enchantment.name: scroll of grand enchantment
scroll_of_grand_enchantment.lore: Thetis found Hephaestus sweating at his bellows, making twenty tripods on golden wheels that would roll to the gods' feasts and home again unaided. Maids of gold who could think and speak held him by the arm as he limped to greet her. Whatever is worn, this working sends through his forge.

scroll_of_stone.name: scroll of stone
scroll_of_stone.lore: Five Amorite kings fled from Joshua down the pass of Beth-horon, and great stones fell on their army out of the sky. The book says more died by the hailstones than by the sword. A stone-caller's rite repeats the day on a small scale. Rock drops on every enemy in sight, harder the sharper the reader's mind.

scroll_of_earth.name: scroll of earth
scroll_of_earth.lore: Korah and his company rose against Moses in the desert. Moses said that if these men died a common death he had not been sent. The ground split under their tents, swallowed them alive with all they owned, and closed. This rite opens the roof instead of the floor. Boulders fall on all in view.

scroll_of_cataclysm.name: scroll of cataclysm
scroll_of_cataclysm.lore: Typhon had a hundred serpent heads and stood taller than the mountains, and the gods fled from him as far as Egypt. Zeus fought him across the world and finally threw Mount Etna on top of him. The smoke is his breath. This working drops a mountainside on everything the reader can see.

scroll_of_smiting.name: scroll of smiting
scroll_of_smiting.lore: Nadab and Abihu, sons of Aaron, filled their censers and offered before the Lord a fire he had not commanded. Fire came out from his presence and consumed them where they stood, and Aaron held his peace. The rite is short. A white flash takes a few of the weakest creatures in sight.

scroll_of_annihilation.name: scroll of annihilation
scroll_of_annihilation.lore: At midnight in Egypt the Destroyer went through the land, house by house. Where lamb's blood marked the doorposts it passed over. Where there was none it took the firstborn, and there was a great cry. This rite sends something like it through a room. Half of what stands in sight, the lesser half, is gone.

scroll_of_extinction.name: scroll of extinction
scroll_of_extinction.lore: Sennacherib of Assyria camped before Jerusalem with an army that had already taken forty-six walled towns. In one night the angel of the Lord went through the camp, and in the morning a hundred and eighty-five thousand lay dead. The king went home. Only the very mightiest are still standing when this rite ends.

scroll_of_purge.name: scroll of purge
scroll_of_purge.lore: The legend is set in 1284: a piper in many-coloured clothes came to Hamelin and offered to deal with its rats. He played, and every rat in the town followed him into the river Weser and drowned. This working plays one tune. The commonest kind of creature in sight leaves the floor entirely.

scroll_of_genocide.name: scroll of genocide
scroll_of_genocide.lore: Ireland has no snakes and never did. The Irish credit Patrick, who is said to have fasted forty days on a mountain in Mayo and then driven every serpent on the island into the sea with his staff. This rite makes a harsher clearance. The two commonest kinds in sight are erased from the floor.

scroll_of_exile.name: scroll of exile
scroll_of_exile.lore: When Pharaoh begged, Moses prayed and the plagues lifted as completely as they had come. The frogs died in the houses and fields. The flies left until not one remained. A west wind carried the locusts into the sea and not a single locust was left in Egypt. Under this working every lesser kind in sight goes the same way.

scroll_of_slow_time.name: scroll of slow time
scroll_of_slow_time.lore: King Hezekiah lay dying and asked for a sign that he would recover. Isaiah offered a choice, and the king asked for the harder thing: the shadow on the stairway of Ahaz went backward ten steps. A chronomancer's lesser rite takes back a few moments in which only the reader moves.

scroll_of_time_stop.name: scroll of time stop
scroll_of_time_stop.lore: Zeno of Elea argued that an arrow in flight occupies, at every instant, a space exactly its own size, and so at every instant is at rest. If it never moves in any instant, when does it move? Philosophers argued for two thousand years. The scroll simply agrees with him for a time.

scroll_of_timeless.name: scroll of timeless
scroll_of_timeless.lore: Joshua needed daylight to finish the battle at Gibeon, and he spoke in the sight of all Israel. The sun stood still over Gibeon and the moon over the valley of Aijalon for about a whole day. There has been no day like it. The great working gives its reader a long stretch of that stillness.

scroll_of_power.name: scroll of power
scroll_of_power.lore: Milo of Croton won the wrestling at six Olympic Games. The story of his training is that he lifted a newborn calf onto his shoulders every day until it was a full-grown bull. The rite compresses his years into a reading. The reader's three weakest faculties are raised, and they stay raised.

scroll_of_greater_power.name: scroll of greater power
scroll_of_greater_power.lore: In the fifth century Martianus Capella wrote an allegory in which seven bridesmaids each present one art: Grammar, Logic, Rhetoric, Geometry, Arithmetic, Astronomy, Music. Schools taught those seven for the next thousand years. The rite is a whole education at a sitting. Nearly every faculty of the reader is raised for good.

scroll_of_great_power.name: scroll of great power
scroll_of_great_power.lore: About the year 270 Porphyry of Tyre wrote a short introduction to Aristotle's logic. It sorted everything that exists into a branching tree, from substance down to Socrates, and students copied it out for a thousand years. This is the tree in full. Every faculty the reader has is permanently raised.

dead_sea_scroll.name: Dead Sea Scroll
dead_sea_scroll.unidentified_name: a brittle parchment sealed in a clay jar
dead_sea_scroll.lore: Sealed in a clay jar in a cave near the sea for two thousand years. What was written on it is not what makes it powerful -- that it survived at all is. Read it and the shape of the whole dungeon is preserved in your mind the same way -- the walls, the corridors, the stairs, if not the shadows that walk between them.

scroll_of_the_labyrinth.name: Scroll of the Labyrinth
scroll_of_the_labyrinth.lore: Sealed with the mark of the Cretan Labyrinth. A reward scroll from Dad -- show him this code!

scroll_of_the_gorgon.name: Scroll of the Gorgon
scroll_of_the_gorgon.lore: Sealed with a serpent's eye. A reward scroll from Dad -- show him this code!

scroll_of_the_hoard.name: Scroll of the Dragon Hoard
scroll_of_the_hoard.lore: Sealed with a golden dragon scale. A reward scroll from Dad -- show him this code!

scroll_of_ragnarok.name: Scroll of Ragnarok
scroll_of_ragnarok.lore: Sealed with the howl of the World-Wolf. A reward scroll from Dad -- show him this code!

scroll_of_the_abyss.name: Scroll of the Abyss
scroll_of_the_abyss.lore: Sealed with the mark of the Bottomless Pit. A reward scroll from Dad -- show him this code!

scroll_of_arachne.name: Scroll of Arachne
scroll_of_arachne.lore: Sealed with a strand of unbreakable silk. A reward scroll from Dad -- show him this code!

scroll_of_lamia.name: Scroll of Lamia
scroll_of_lamia.lore: Sealed with a serpent's tear. A reward scroll from Dad -- show him this code!

scroll_of_talos.name: Scroll of Talos
scroll_of_talos.lore: Sealed with molten bronze. A reward scroll from Dad -- show him this code!

scroll_of_echidna.name: Scroll of Echidna
scroll_of_echidna.lore: Sealed with the mark of the Mother of Monsters. A reward scroll from Dad -- show him this code!

scroll_of_the_erlking.name: Scroll of the Erlking
scroll_of_the_erlking.lore: Sealed with a frozen leaf that never wilts. A reward scroll from Dad -- show him this code!

scroll_of_camazotz.name: Scroll of Camazotz
scroll_of_camazotz.lore: Sealed with a bat's wing pressed in wax. A reward scroll from Dad -- show him this code!

scroll_of_cacus.name: Scroll of Cacus

scroll_of_nine_hells.name: Scroll of the Nine Hells
scroll_of_nine_hells.unidentified_name: a scroll bound with blood-red wax
scroll_of_nine_hells.lore: Dante counted nine circles in his Inferno, narrowing like a funnel to the frozen lake at the bottom, and set a different ruin in each. Nine seals close this vellum, one for every circle, pressed in wax the colour of old blood by the demon Asmodeus. Broken together, they unmake every lesser creature in sight. The mightiest stand untouched.
scroll_of_nine_hells.design_notes: Asmodeus L92 boss reward. Wired via monster.treasure.boss_scroll_id.

scroll_of_chromatic_doom.name: Scroll of Chromatic Doom
scroll_of_chromatic_doom.unidentified_name: a scroll shifting through five colors
scroll_of_chromatic_doom.lore: In the Babylonian creation poem Tiamat is the salt sea, mother of the first gods. When they killed her husband she bore eleven monsters and went to war. Marduk caught her in a net, split her like a dried fish, and made the sky from one half. Dragon-lore gave her five heads and five colours. This scroll speaks for all five at once, and nothing lesser in sight outlives it.
scroll_of_chromatic_doom.design_notes: Tiamat L85 boss reward. Wired via monster.treasure.boss_scroll_id.
